answer: A sybil swarm stalls when each newcomer must earn a jetty mooring licence before trading. First, it registers one identity, posts a 50-token bond, and completes four supervised deliveries along a river route. Second, two captains stamp each arrival at the jetty after checking its logs. Third, its quota rises only after thirty clean days, and fraud burns the bond and bars it for ninety days. One fake costs about $780 in bonds and work, while 1,000 fakes need $780,000 and 8,000 hours of staged deliveries. Like a sonnet earned line by line, trust is built slowly, not claimed in bulk.
